newsitem.title: USA: CNS Inc may not reach Q2 net of $0.17/shr.
newsitem.headline: CNS Inc may not reach Q2 net of $0.17/shr.

text.p: CNS Inc President and Chief Operating Officer Richard Jahnke said Wednesday the company may not reach second-quarter earnings of $0.17 per share, but it may exceed $0.71 a share for all of 1997.
"I thought the (analysts') consensus (for the quarter) was a little lower than ($0.17)," Jahnke told Reuters at the company's annual meeting.

"I think we're going to see good growth in our U.S. business, but in our international business there's still a big question mark about what will happen in this year's second quarter compared to (1996)," he said.

CNS, which markets the Breathe Right nasal strip, posted net income of $3.0 million, or $0.15 a share, in the second quarter of last year, which included $8 million in international sales, Jahnke said.
Jahnke said he expects the international sales to fall short of the 1996 figure.

"International revenues are going to be much less than they were a year ago because they've just done the pipeline fill," he said. "So you've got to sell it off the shelves before (merchants) can buy to restock."
Earlier this month, CNS reported net income of $1.3 million, or $0.07 a share in the first quarter, versus $3.1 million, or $0.17 a year ago.
With regard to full-year results, Jahnke said analysts' estimates of $0.71 a share are "at the conservative end of the range."
CNS reported net income of $15.5 million, or $0.78 a share, in 1996 on sales $85.9 million.

"It sounds like for the analysts to be at that ($0.71), and where they are in the second quarter, there's probably some timing of international business that has to go into their estimates," Jahnke said. "We believe (exceeding $0.71 a share) is certainly possible."
Jahnke said 1997 revenues may be in the $78-million to $78.4-million range.

"We expect our second and third-quarter revenues to dip as they have in the past because you lose the seasonal users and then pick up in the fourth quarter," Jahnke said. "The analysts' estimates (for $78-million to $78.4 million in 1997 revenues) are appropriate at this time."

Jahnke also told shareholders that the company earlier this week had requested approval from the U.S. Food Drug Administration to market the Breathe Right strips as having the ability to improve athletic performance.
Later this week, CNS will also seek FDA approval to market the strips as having the ability to improve sleep by reducing snoring and congestion, Jahnke said.
"We hope both of these claims are given FDA approval yet this year," Jahnke said.
Jahnke said new product launches by the end are possible.

"There's nothing planned for introduction int he second quarter this year. Depending upon the results on the clinical trials that are about to begin on some products, there are some that could come out as early as the end of this year."
Company officials declined to give specifics on any of its potential new products.
CNS shares closed unchanged Wednesday at 9-1/8.
